sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
The player's pixel count isn't 36 (the pink square is probably 36 pixels but might include the white center — the M pixels are only the border: 6x6 border = 36-4=32... let's stop caring).
Key data:
- Transition 0 RIGHT: rope row 38, tip 28. Player rows ~36-41?? Wait, rope row 38! Initial rope row 38 → player rows 36-41. Hmm, but in the initial image the player looked like it was in the middle. Corridor rows 15-45. Player rows 36-41.
- Transition 1 UP: rope row 32 (player 30-35).
- Transition 4 RIGHT: rope row 32, tip 46. Blocks: green rows 31-34! So at transition 4 the rope passed through green (rope row 32 is within green 31-34). Green legend: no change.
- Transition 7 UP: rope row 20 (player 18-23).
- Transition 8 RIGHT: rope row 20, tip 46 → passes through red (19-22) → red goes hollow.
- Transition 14 RIGHT: rope row 32, tip 46 → passes through green again → green still filled.
So green was passed twice (transitions 4 and 14) and never went hollow; red was passed once and went hollow.
Blue: was the rope ever on the blue row (26)? Transition 6 UP: rope 26, tip 40 — no extension. So blue was never passed.
So: green passed twice → no hollow. Red passed once → hollow.
What's different between red and green?!
- Red is at the top (rows 19-22), green is at the bottom (31-34).
- Player position when passing: red → player 18-23 (topmost); green → player 30-35 (middle).
- Rope length when passing: both 40→46.
Hypothesis A: hollow only when player is at the topmost position.
Hypothesis B: hollow only for the topmost block (red).
These are hard to distinguish... but they're equivalent for red. For the game to be solvable, green and blue must also be collectable somehow.
Hmm, wait — maybe I'm thinking about it backwards. Maybe the hollow isn't "collected" but a "warning": the rope is currently penetrating the block (contact state). Green is currently penetrated (tip 46, rope row 32 within green 31-34) yet green is filled. So the contact theory is dead... unless the contact requires the tip to be inside the block (not past it). Tip 46 is past both red and green.
OK, yet another thought: maybe the hollow red in the legend is a "next target" indicator that appears when the rope is extended to max length (46) on that block's row. And the reason green didn't go hollow is... the rope was already at 46? No, it was 40→46.
Hmm, let's look at the actual frame of transition 8 and check whether the board's red block changed (e.g., a white dot appeared in the center of the block). The animation showed R>W only in the legend. So no.
Let me try a different approach: brute-force experimentation with a cheap discriminating test:
Test 1: Extend the rope to 46 on the blue row (player 24-29). If blue goes hollow → hollow = "extended to max on that row" (and green's failure was a fluke/ordering). If blue doesn't go hollow → hollow is special to red (topmost).
This test costs: from current (rope 32, tip 46, player 30-35): ACTION7 (46→40), UP (player 24-29), RIGHT (40→46 on blue row). 3 actions. Then check the legend.
If blue goes hollow: next test green with the same procedure (ACTION7, DOWN, RIGHT) — if green goes hollow this time, then the earlier green failure was because... the rope was already at 46? No, it was 40→46. Hmm, or because green was already "seen"?
Actually wait — maybe hollow means "the first block the rope reaches at max extension on that row" — i.e., a per-row "first reach" event. Green was reached at max on transition 4 (40→46) — should have gone hollow then. It didn't.
Let's just run the blue test. Actually, let's also reconsider the possibility that hollow = "the block the rope is currently touching" and that green's legend rendering is different (the N color renders differently?). The red legend when hollow: 'RWWRRWWR' — R W W R / R W W R. If green went hollow it should be 'NWWNNWWN'. Currently 'NNNNNNNN'. So no.
Run the blue test: ACTION7, UP, RIGHT.

sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>

def legend(f):
    a=f.ascii.split('\n')
    r58,r59=a[58],a[59]
    return {"red":r58[27:31]+r59[27:31], "green":r58[33:37]+r59[33:37], "blue":r58[39:43]+r59[39:43]}
r=action(['ACTION7','UP','RIGHT'],intent='explore')
print("legend now:", legend(current_frame))
print("result:", {k:last_action_result.get(k) for k in ('board_changed','gameplay_changed','no_impact','level_completed','done','game_over')})
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
